content.value_statement: Large changes are hard to verify and often create new defects. This skill guides small improvements, error proofing, standard patterns, and just-in-time design.
actual_capabilities: Guides incremental implementation and refactoring decisions.
Encourages validation, guards, and type-safe designs.
Promotes consistency with existing codebase patterns.
Helps avoid premature abstraction and optimization.
Frames reviews around small, verifiable improvements.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not execute checks automatically.
It does not replace project tests, linters, or type checks.
It depends on available context from the current codebase.
It may need project-specific standards to be supplied.

use_cases.title: Refine a Feature Safely
use_cases.description: Break a feature into small changes, verify each step, and avoid unnecessary scope growth.

use_cases.title: Review Code for Preventable Errors
use_cases.description: Identify validation gaps, invalid states, and inconsistent patterns before the change ships.

use_cases.title: Improve Team Engineering Standards
use_cases.description: Turn repeated lessons into clear patterns, documentation, and quality gates.

prompt_templates.title: Find One Improvement
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this change using Kaizen. Suggest one small improvement that improves quality without expanding scope.

prompt_templates.title: Error Proof a Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply Poka-Yoke to this workflow. Identify invalid states, missing validation, and safer defaults.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Incremental Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a step-by-step refactor plan. Keep each step small, testable, and reversible.

prompt_templates.title: Standardize a Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this approach with existing project patterns. Recommend a standard and explain when to use it.

output_examples.input: Review a payment change for safer validation.
output: Use a required positive amount type where possible.
Keep the first change focused on validation only.

output_examples.input: Plan a refactor for duplicated API client logic.
output: Start by matching the existing client pattern.
Extract shared behavior only after repeated use is clear.
Verify each step with current tests before continuing.

output_examples.input: Assess whether to add a generic framework.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend solving the current case first, then abstracting only after multiple proven use cases.

best_practices: Ask for the smallest useful improvement first.
Provide current tests and project conventions when available.
Verify each change before adding another improvement.
anti_patterns: Requesting a broad rewrite before defining the immediate problem.
Adding abstractions for possible future requirements.
Using the skill as a substitute for testing or security review.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps improve code through incremental changes, error prevention, consistent patterns, and focused scope.

faq.question: Does it modify code by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance that an AI coding assistant can apply during implementation or review.

faq.question: Is it only for refactoring?
faq.answer: No. It also supports design decisions, validation strategy, process improvement, and review feedback.

faq.question: How should I use it with Claude or Codex?
faq.answer: Ask Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to apply Kaizen while reviewing a change or planning implementation.

faq.question: Can it replace automated checks?
faq.answer: No. Use tests, type checks, linters, and security tools alongside this guidance.

faq.question: What context improves results?
faq.answer: Share the current goal, codebase conventions, test status, and any constraints on scope or timing.
